Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: operator-step note for #8330 (merging the host-only `.claude/` paths on a superseded PR)

**Planning ref:** `git rev-parse HEAD` = `a9a3f6bcb8dc8f3041a7c3486e37d4c2d7ce3442`, resolved checkout ref `main`, symbolic branch `main`. The PLANNING REF CONTEXT line `Integration branch mismatch:` reads `unknown`, not `true`, so there is no mismatch block.

**Clarification mapping:** no questions were asked, and `/answer [auto-answered-by-clarify]` was posted automatically. The scope comes from the unblock fix-up body alone: record an operator step behind `PR8330_SUPERSEDED_HOST_MERGE_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP`, add no runtime code, and gate no existing path.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends PUSH_DESTINATION_GUARD_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP
Scope-mode justification: The fix-up says "No runtime code". The only deliverable is a durable, readable record of the one manual step that remains: a person merges the host-only `.claude/` paths on branch `claude/great-ride-4jmlxv` (PR #8330). The record reuses the convention the repo already uses for steps the pipeline cannot perform. Examples are the `PUSH_DESTINATION_GUARD_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP`, `MERGE_GUARD_LIVE_PARITY_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` and `IMPLEMENTS_MARKER_CLAUDE_MD_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` paragraphs in `agents.md`, which landed as `agents.d/` fragments with a `changelog.d/` entry. Adding a reader of the placeholder in any script would make the change bigger and would gate nothing useful. It would also break the rule that existing paths keep running unchanged. The complete option (an agents fragment plus a changelog fragment) costs only a few lines more than a fragment alone, so it wins under §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed). The placeholder name must appear outside `CHANGELOG.md` and `changelog.d/`. The unblock judge's `placeholder_retired` hold uses `git grep` to decide the step is done when that name disappears from the default branch (`agents.md`, "Unblock judge `wait` verdict and operator-step holds"). So the agents fragment is what keeps #8330 held until a person acts.

## Files likely to change

- `agents.d/8330-superseded-host-merge-operator-step.md` (new)
- `changelog.d/8330-superseded-host-merge-operator-step.md` (new)

## Automation surface (§20.E)

- **New script, extended script or existing code only:** none of these. This is a docs-only change made of two new fragments, with no new script and no code changes.
- **Scheduler or PR-push entry point:** none is added.
  - The existing release-time fold (`scripts/assemble_agents.py` from the release workflows) folds the agents fragment into `agents.md`. CI already checks it: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 258–259 run `assemble_agents.py check` and `tests/test_agents_fragment_contract.py`.
  - The existing unblock judge `placeholder_retired` hold (`scripts/unblock_judge.sh`) watches the placeholder.
- **New long-running supervisor (§20.C):** none.
- **DB work (§20.D):** none.
- **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry (§20.F):** none needed, because no script or supervisor is introduced. The placeholder is retired by deleting the fragment paragraph, as `WRAPPED_GIT_WRITE_GUARD_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` was.

## Functions or modules to implement

There are no functions. The two fragments are below.

1. **`agents.d/8330-superseded-host-merge-operator-step.md`**
   - It is a single block under `<!-- agents: section="Workflow architecture" -->`. That section exists at agents.md L39 and already holds the sibling `*_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` paragraphs at L873–905 and L1011. No ` new` marker is used.
   - Model the wording on the `PUSH_DESTINATION_GUARD_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` and `MERGE_GUARD_LIVE_PARITY_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` paragraphs. The paragraph states these points:
     - **The placeholder does nothing.** `PR8330_SUPERSEDED_HOST_MERGE_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` is an unset placeholder for a pending operator step. No workflow, script or test reads it, and setting it changes nothing. Releases, tagging, dispatches and merges run as before.
     - **Origin.** It comes from unblock round 1 on #8330 (stop `needs-human`). Review/autofix failed twice on head `d738910` with `conflict_resolver_sandbox_path_host_only`: the conflict resolver refuses host-executed `.claude/` paths by design, and no pipeline phase may write them.
     - **Why the PR conflicts.** `main` already carries the same feature from #8323. That includes:
       - `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py` and its live copy `.claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py`
       - `tests/test_safe_fetch_url.py`
       - the converted `/investigate-issue`, `/analyze-log` and `/apply-url` command templates and live copies
       - the `ci.yml` step that runs the test (around line 777–779)
       - `agents.d/8323-safe-fetch-url-helper.md` and `changelog.d/8323-safe-fetch-url-commands.md`

       Every file the PR touches therefore hits an add/add or edit/edit conflict.
     - **The step.** In a trusted interactive checkout, an operator merges the default branch into `claude/great-ride-4jmlxv` and resolves the conflicts by hand, including the host-only `.claude/` paths.
       - Main's #8323 content is the baseline. Keep a PR-side difference only if it is deliberate.
       - Keep each `.claude/` file byte-identical to its `workflow-templates/.claude/` twin, so `tests/test_claude_template_live_parity.py` stays green.
       - Keep `tests/test_safe_fetch_url.py` green, and keep the commands' literal `python scripts/safe_fetch_url.py` invocation unchanged, because the consumer test looks for that text.
     - **What not to do.** Do not add the files to `.github/ai/claude_template_divergence.json`. Do not relax or bypass the parity test. Do not ask a pipeline phase or `override_guard` to write `.claude/**`.
     - **Retirement.** Once PR #8330 merges or closes with no host-only conflict left, remove this paragraph and retire the placeholder as `WRAPPED_GIT_WRITE_GUARD_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` was retired.
     - **No editor authority.** The note does not authorize any editor to touch `.claude/**`.

2. **`changelog.d/8330-superseded-host-merge-operator-step.md`**
   - The first line is `<!-- changelog: changed -->`, a category that already exists (32 fragments use it).
   - It is one bold-headline bullet in the style of the CHANGELOG entries for 7053 and 7254, following `docs/changelog-style.md`. It says PR #8330 waits for an operator to merge its host-only `.claude/` paths because `main` already carries #8323. It names the placeholder and the fragment, and states that nothing reads the placeholder: no setting changes, and the helper, commands, CI and tests are untouched.
   - It uses no auto-close keyword next to any issue number (§21); it says "Refs #8330" or just names the PR.

## Data structures affected

None. There are no JSON, DB, label or marker changes.

## API or interface changes

None. The new env-var name is a documentation placeholder with no reader. It does not collide with anything: no file in the working tree names `PR8330_` or `great-ride`.

## Decisions

### D1 — Record the step as an agents.d fragment, with no code reading the placeholder
- Chosen: a docs-only fragment naming `PR8330_SUPERSEDED_HOST_MERGE_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP`, which no code reads.
- Alternatives considered: (a) add a check that reads the placeholder in `scripts/unblock_judge.sh` or `scripts/operator_step_issue.py`; (b) edit `agents.md` directly; (c) write the `.claude/` merge resolution from the pipeline.
- Why: the fix-up says "No runtime code", and any reader would risk gating an existing path. §25 forbids direct additions to `agents.md`. Option (c) is forbidden: the resolver refuses host-only paths, and pipeline editors cannot write `.claude/**`.

### D2 — Put the fragment in "Workflow architecture"
- Chosen: `section="Workflow architecture"`.
- Alternatives considered: "Interactive slash-command model selection", which holds "Live `.claude/` copies and their templates" at L2790; "Utility helpers", where the #8323 helper is documented.
- Why: the sibling operator-step placeholder paragraphs (L873–905, L1011) already live in "Workflow architecture", so operators find all pending steps in one place.

### D3 — Add a changelog fragment as well
- Chosen: also add `changelog.d/8330-…md` with category `changed`.
- Alternatives considered: no changelog entry, since the change is docs-only.
- Why: earlier operator-step notes (7053, 7254, 7765) each got a changelog line telling operators that nothing changes. The `placeholder_retired` check ignores `changelog.d/`, so this entry does not affect the hold.

## Security considerations

- **Trust boundaries:** none are touched at runtime. The change keeps the boundary that stops pipeline phases writing host-executed `.claude/**` files. The note states that it grants no editor authority.
- **Authorization:** no new endpoint or surface. The operator step is done only by a person in a trusted interactive checkout.
- **External input:** none is read. The PR head (`shubhodeep1/coding-workflows`, `d738910…`) is treated as untrusted. The note tells the operator to use main's #8323 content as the baseline, so unreviewed changes on the PR side do not slip into the host-only `.claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py`, which protects against SSRF.
- **Abuse cases:**
  - Someone could cite the note to justify a pipeline write to `.claude/**`. Its explicit wording blocks this.
  - Someone could add an allowlist entry to `.github/ai/claude_template_divergence.json` to get past the parity check. The note forbids this.
- **Secrets and money:** no secrets, and nothing money-related.

## Potential risks or edge cases

- **The hold depends on the placeholder name.** `placeholder_retired` searches the default branch with `git grep`. The name must stay in the agents fragment, and later in `agents.md` after the fold, until the operator acts. Removing
